message:
Some of your response relates to New Tech vs. Old Tech, I think. Consider how much has been spent on buying and cataloguing all the books in the campus  library.  Would you want to routinely press students to move from activity to activity there?  Or would casual browsing be OK  sometimes?  But we don't think about all that paper capital in the way we do about silicon chip capital.  I've often called refrigeration the invisible technology.  It's impacted our lives just about as much as the automobile  and the computer--maybe more in health and nutrition, but we never discuss the energy costs of cooling and freezing our food and cooling our workspaces.

Anyway, it's good to shift activities.  I try to give no  more than 20 minutes to any single class activity, because that's the point the research suggests many minds are wandering.  But I've also  used the computer lab (usually later in the term) to let students work at their  own pace, for both searching and writing.
